m-kremenets.note: Closed after the 1830-31 insurrection; transfer to Kyiv in 1832.

m-zadar.note: Granted the status of a privileged university with the right to confer doctorates in 1553.

u-prague-1348-founding.note: Clement VI's privilege 1347; Charles IV's charter 7 April 1348.

u-prague-1366-charter.note: College for twelve masters (Collegium Caroli) founded 1366.

u-prague-1409-reform.note: Decree issued 18 January 1409; departing Germans founded Leipzig.

u-prague-1419-destruction.note: Only the arts faculty continued until the early 17th century.

u-prague-1784-reform.note: Some sources date German instruction to 1774.

u-krakow-1370-destruction.note: Ceased after the king's death; teaching resumed 1391 through Jadwiga's efforts.

u-krakow-1853-reform.note: German became the language of instruction after Kraków's incorporation into Austria in 1846.

u-krakow-1870-reform.note: Source confirms Polish restored under autonomy without exact year.

u-pecs-1367-founding.note: Bull of 1 September 1367, issued at Viterbo.

u-pecs-1390-destruction.note: Declined after Louis I's death (1382); may have lingered into the early 15th century.

fix.desc: Pope John XXIII signed the deed of re-establishment on 1 August 1410 at Sigismund's request.

u-obuda-1410-refoundation.note: Probably closed after the 1403 revolt; refounded 1 August 1410.

fix.desc: Pope Paul II authorised the university on 29 May 1465; it opened on 20 July 1467.

u-pozsony-1465-founding.note: Bull dated 29 May 1465 (some give 19 May); opened 20 July 1467.

u-pozsony-1490-destruction.note: Activity ceased after Matthias's death in 1490; decline earlier.

u-vilnius-1579-founding.note: Báthory's privilege 1 April 1579; papal approval 30 October 1579.

fix.desc: Charles XI reopened the university in Dorpat in 1690.

u-dorpat-1690-refoundation.note: The name Academia Gustavo-Carolina is attached to the 1699 reopening in Pärnu.

u-dorpat-1699-relocation.note: Reopened in Pärnu on 28 August 1699 as Academia Gustavo-Carolina.

u-dorpat-1802-refoundation.note: Reopened April 1802; act of foundation confirmed 12 December 1802.

u-dorpat-1889-reform.note: Russian became the language of instruction in 1895.

u-olomouc-1642-destruction.note: Swedish occupation under Torstensson lasted eight years.

u-olomouc-1855-reform.note: Philosophy closed 1851, law 1855; university closed in 1860 except theology.

t-moscow-navigation-1701-founding.note: Founding declaration of 14 January 1701; Magnitsky appointed February 1701.

u-kazan-1819-reform.note: Curator Magnitsky's period 1819-1826 saw dismissals and departures.

u-kosice-1660-charter.note: Leopold I's permission 1660; opened that year with two faculties.

j-cluj-1603-destruction.note: Sources record the Jesuits' expulsion by the Transylvanian diet in 1588 and a final ban around 1607; a townspeople's expulsion in 1603 is not confirmed by these sources.

t-st-petersburg-mining-1773-founding.note: Founded 21 October (1 November) 1773; first students enrolled June 1774.

t-st-petersburg-mining-1833-reform.note: Called Institute of the Corps of Mining Engineers from 1834.

b-moscow-academy-1687-founding.note: The brothers arrived in 1685 and founded the academy; 1687 is the conventional opening date.

u-kyiv-1834-founding.note: Opened 1834; library built on the Kremenets Lyceum collection.

fix.desc: After the discovery of a student society linked to Polish conspirators the university was closed for about half a year.

u-kyiv-1839-suppression.note: Closure followed the discovery of a Polish-linked student society in 1838.

u-kyiv-1847-suppression.note: The Brotherhood was founded in late 1845 and crushed in 1847.

u-lviv-1848-destruction.note: Shelled in November 1848; most of the library destroyed.

u-lviv-1871-reform.note: Polish became the administrative language in 1871 and main language of instruction in 1879.

m-nizhyn-1820-founding.note: Endowment of 210,000 rubles from Count Illia Bezborodko.

m-kremenets-1833-suppression.note: Closed after the 1830-31 insurrection; library, collections and staff transferred to Kyiv in 1832.

u-chernivtsi-1897-access.note: Austrian philosophical faculties opened to women in 1897/98.

u-moscow-1755-founding.note: Decree of 12 (23) January 1755; inaugural ceremony 26 April 1755.

m-st-petersburg-medical-1798-founding.note: Paul I's decree of 18 December 1798; built on surgical schools dating from 1733 and 1786.

m-st-petersburg-medical-1872-access.note: Women's course for learned midwives established 1872; Women's Medical Courses from 1876.

fix.desc: Joseph I's rescript of 18 January 1707, at the petition of the Bohemian Estates, approved Willenberg's proposal for public engineering instruction in Prague; Willenberg was appointed the first professor in 1717.

t-prague-1707-founding.note: Rescript 18 January 1707; Willenberg appointed professor in 1717.

t-budapest-1846-reform.note: Joseph College of Technology opened 1846; named Joseph Industrial School after an 1850 merger.

fix.desc: Raised to university rank as the Royal Joseph University of Technology (Királyi József Műegyetem).

t-budapest-1871-reform.note: The name Joseph Polytechnicum dates from 1856; in 1871 it became the Royal Joseph University of Technology.

fix.desc: Opened on 14 October 1862 as a private German-language polytechnic, approved by Alexander II in 1861.

t-riga-1862-founding.note: Opening date given as 14 October 1862 (probably the New Style equivalent of 2 October).

t-riga-1896-reform.note: Change of language of instruction not covered in source.

t-st-petersburg-polytechnic-1899-foundin.note: Decree of 19 February 1899; formal opening 1 October 1902.

t-warsaw-1898-founding.note: Three faculties: mechanics, chemistry, engineering and construction.

t-keszthely-1848-suppression.note: Work was interrupted after the 1848-49 revolution.

t-banska-stiavnica-1762-founding.note: Maria Theresa's decision of 13 December 1762; school opened 1763.

u-warsaw-1831-suppression.note: Ceased fifteen years after its creation, following the defeat of the November Uprising.

u-zagreb-1874-refoundation.note: Founding act ratified 5 January 1874; inaugural ceremony 19 October 1874.

u-cluj-1872-founding.note: Founding laws ratified 12 October 1872; the name Franz Joseph was adopted in 1881.

u-prague-german-1882-founding.note: Retention of the insignia and Carolinum not covered by these sources.

a-sarospatak-1531-founding.note: 1531 is the traditional date of the school's beginnings.

fix.desc: Ottoman forces sacked Gyulafehérvár and the college; the students fled to Kolozsvár.

u-zamosc-1594-founding.note: Some sources date the founding to 1595, the year teaching opened.

a-rakow-1638-suppression.note: The crucifix incident is not covered in these sources.

a-gdansk-1558-founding.note: Exact day not given in source.

a-gdansk-1817-reform.note: Closed 10 November 1817 and incorporated into St Mary's school.

t-st-petersburg-railways-1809-founding.note: First students began classes in November 1810.

b-kharkiv-collegium-1726-founding.note: Founded in Belgorod in 1722 and moved to Kharkiv in 1726.

b-kharkiv-collegium-1817-reform.note: New statute in 1817; the name 'college' was kept until 1841.

u-prague-czech-1897-access.note: Austrian philosophical faculties opened to women in 1897/98; medicine followed in 1900.

u-prague-german-1897-access.note: Austrian philosophical faculties opened to women in 1897/98.

b-iasi-vasiliana-1640-founding.note: Founded 1640 by professors from the Kyiv-Mohyla Academy under Sofronii Pochasky.

a-sarospatak-1650-reform.note: Comenius accepted the invitation to Patak and stayed until summer 1654.

a-sarospatak-1671-confessional.note: The college's exile is dated 1672-1703 in the college's own history.

b-moscow-academy-1701-reform.note: Peter I made it a state academy under Palladius Rogovsky.

b-iasi-academy-1707-founding.note: Founded 1707 under Antioh Cantemir; re-established 1714 by Nicolae Mavrocordat.

m-yaroslavl-1803-founding.note: Decree of 18 June 1803 approving Pavel Demidov's endowment.

m-zadar-1807-suppression.note: Abolished by the French government on 8 January 1807.

fix.title: Closed on the French departure
fix.desc: The écoles centrales ended with the departure of the French in 1813, and the earlier lyceum system was restored.

u-ljubljana-1813-suppression.note: The schools ended with the French withdrawal in 1813.

b-moscow-academy-1814-reform.note: Became the Ecclesiastical Academy at the Trinity-Sergius Lavra in 1814.

m-odessa-richelieu-1817-founding.note: Origin in the Noble Institute not covered in source.

u-vilnius-1823-suppression.note: Novosiltsev's investigation of the Philomaths and Philarets; Mickiewicz arrested 1823 and deported 1824; Lelewel deprived of his chair in 1824.

t-marymont-1831-suppression.note: Closed after the November Uprising; one source gives activity 1816-1830.

u-st-petersburg-1835-reform.note: The 1835 statute applied to all universities of the empire and strengthened central control.

u-moscow-1835-reform.note: The 1835 statute applied to all universities of the empire and strengthened central control.

u-kazan-1835-reform.note: The 1835 statute applied to all universities of the empire and strengthened central control.

fix.desc: Renamed the Alexander Lyceum in 1843 and transferred to St Petersburg on 1 January 1844.

m-tsarskoye-selo-1843-relocation.note: Renamed 1843; moved to St Petersburg on 1 January 1844.

u-st-petersburg-1861-suppression.note: Closed after student disturbances in autumn 1861.

u-st-petersburg-1863-reform.note: The 1863 statute restored election of rectors, deans and professors at all imperial universities.

u-moscow-1863-reform.note: The 1863 statute restored election of rectors, deans and professors at all imperial universities.

t-banska-stiavnica-1867-reform.note: Became a Hungarian state institution after the 1867 Compromise; Hungarian became the language of instruction in 1868.

m-yaroslavl-1868-reform.note: Interim statute of the Demidov Juridical Lyceum signed 15 July 1868.

u-st-petersburg-1884-reform.note: The 1884 statute returned appointments to the minister and banned student organisations across the empire.
